conviction_note: Two forces of similar size and opposite sign. (1) Fundamentals point down: Q3 fuel came in about $0.15-0.19/gal above AAL's $3.75 assumption, going by Alaska ($3.94 against the same $3.75) and United ($3.90). Q4 fuel will be guided near $4.7-4.8 (UAL $4.80, ALK $4.65-4.85; AAL's CFO said +$1/gal on 16 Sept), so the FY -$0.65/+$0.65 guide is very likely cut. (2) The reaction template points up: UAL rose about 5-7% on 21 Oct on a Q4 guide 43% below consensus, because Q4 revenue growth of more than 20% shows fares passing fuel through. AAL's put skew (+4.5 vol pts, put/call OI 3.68) already pays for the downside. The findings net to about +0.2 and the scaled number is -0.4: abs 7.0 (the name's median reaction; a new Q4 guide and an FY cut are likely) and p_up 47. The gap is small and comes from AAL's own record of selling fuel-driven guide cuts (-8.3% in July 2026), which keeps p_up just under 50.

Consensus sits at the top of the revenue range and above the EPS midpoint (-$0.40). No sourced AAL Q4 or FY consensus was found, so the guidance findings are capped.

findings.finding: Q3 fuel very likely came in above AAL's $3.75/gal guide assumption: Alaska, which also assumed $3.75, reported $3.94, and United reported $3.90. AAL's CFO puts each 1c/gal at about $10m a quarter, so $0.15-0.19 above plan is about $150-190m, or roughly $0.23-0.29 a share, against the guide. Consensus of -$0.28 already sits above the -$0.40 guide midpoint, so it assumes revenue at the top of the +16-19% range will offset that fuel cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (23 Jul): an adjusted EPS beat ($0.15 against about $0.03) was sold -8.3% on the guide cut. Q1 2026: a beat on the adjusted loss (-$0.40 against -$0.47) gave +2.4% on the baseline window (about +5% intraday per press). The reported quarter has mattered less than the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Zacks shows a -2.66% Earnings ESP and consensus revisions down sharply over 60 days, so the street knows fuel ran hot. But a consensus of -$0.28, above the guide midpoint, implies analysts expect revenue upside to absorb all of it. If the market had fully priced the fuel overrun, consensus would sit at or below -$0.40.
findings.independence: United Q3 fuel $3.90/gal (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000184/ual_erx09302026xex991.htm). On the offsetting side, AAL's CEO said on 16 Sept that he felt 'really good' about +16-19% revenue (https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/09/16/breaking-news/american-and-united-prepare-capacity-cuts-over-fuel-costs/). Proxy: peer fuel, not AAL's own number.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide and the FY 2026 guide (-$0.65 to +$0.65, implied Q4 midpoint about +$0.65 after Q1 -$0.40, Q2 +$0.15 and a Q3 midpoint of -$0.40) will absorb a large fuel step-up. AAL's CFO said on 16 Sept 2026 that Q4 fuel was running about $1/gal above the July assumption, about $1bn of extra cost. Peers have since guided Q4 fuel at $4.80 (United, which said this is about 45c above the street's fuel deck) and $4.65-4.85 (Alaska, which guided a Q4 loss of -$2.50 to -$2.00). At about 1.05bn Q4 gallons, a 45c gap to the street's deck is about $470m, roughly $0.70 a share for AAL before fare recapture, so the Q4 guide and a cut FY range likely land below current models.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AAL has sold fuel-driven guide cuts hard: -8.3% on 2026-07-23 (FY cut to -$0.65/+$0.65 despite a Q2 beat). The baseline's Jan/Jul prints (-7.0%, -9.6%, -8.7%) were also negative and its Oct/Apr prints positive (+5.6%, +2.4%, +3.1%), though the season pattern is not established.
findings.why_not_priced: The CFO's +$1/gal is public, and UAL's statement that its $4.80 sits 45c above the street deck says sell-side fuel assumptions lag the curve. If AAL's Q4 consensus had been rebased to about $4.80 fuel, analysts would be sitting on a Q4 loss and an FY loss well below the guide's midpoint, and no source found shows that. No sourced AAL Q4/FY consensus was found, so this is capped. The put skew of +4.5 already pays for downside, which is why this is sized below the July reaction.
findings.independence: UAL Q4 fuel $4.80, 45c above the consensus deck (https://www.aol.com/articles/united-airlines-forecasts-fourth-quarter-200743000.html, 2026-10-20). Alaska Q4 fuel $4.65-4.85 and a Q4 loss guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000766421/000076642126000046/ex99110202026earningsrelea.htm). Delta Q4 fuel about $4.25 (refinery offset) and FY cut to $5.10-5.60 (https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx). Gulf Coast jet spot peaked at $4.705 on 15 Sept and was $4.399 on 29 Sept (https://www.flycraft.com/jet-fuel-price).

findings.finding: The peer reaction template this week is that fuel-driven guide misses are being looked through when revenue pass-through is visible. United guided Q4 adjusted EPS to $0.50-1.50 against $1.76 consensus (midpoint 43% below) with Q4 revenue growth over 20% and 72% fuel recapture, and its stock rose about 4.9-6.9% on 21 Oct. Delta fell only about 3% on 9 Oct after cutting FY EPS from $6.50-7.50 to $5.10-5.60. AAL, at 30% below its 52-week high with puts heavily bid, can see a guide in line with peers' trigger the same relief.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2026 the peer read did not save AAL (-8.3%). In Oct 2025 AAL rose +5.6% on its print. AAL tends to move about 1.2-1.5x UAL on sector news (high beta, levered), which is not sourced here and is an inference.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: AAL is +7% over 5 days and rallied with UAL today, the baseline sealed at 17:11 UTC. But the option market still pays +4.5 vol points for puts, with put/call open interest at 3.68. If the market had accepted the UAL template for AAL, the skew would have flattened and the implied move would sit nearer the 7% historical median, not 5.6%.
findings.independence: Investing.com 21 Oct: UAL's Q4 guide was 43% below consensus, Evercore kept its Outperform, and the ticker showed UAL +6.9% (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-united-airlines-stock-sliding-today-93CH-5644458). DAL's -3% on its cut (rttnews above). Shares the UAL guide document with finding 2 (one reads the number, this reads the reaction).

findings.finding: Revenue and capacity support a strong Q4 revenue guide and a better Q3 top line. AAL's CEO said on 16 Sept that revenue strength was broad-based (domestic and international, premium and coach) and that AAL had recaptured 'a tremendous amount' of fuel. AAL is trimming Q4/December capacity and exited six NY-area routes in October. Domestic-heavy peers printed strong numbers: United domestic passenger revenue +19.9% and TRASM +15.9%, Delta domestic unit revenue +16%, Alaska RASM +11.7% (beating) with September yield +17%. Delta and United both guide Q4 revenue about +20% or more.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: record revenue +16.3% did not stop a -8.3% move, because fuel guidance dominated. Q1 2026: record revenue plus a beat bought about +2.4-5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus of $16.2bn already sits at the top of AAL's Q3 range, so Q3 revenue is largely priced. What is not obviously priced is a Q4 revenue guide near +20%, since AAL's Q3 guide was +16-19% on +3-5% capacity, and Q4 capacity is being cut. If it were priced, the downside skew would be smaller.
findings.independence: United domestic +19.9% and TRASM +15.9% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000184/ual_erx09302026xex991.htm). Delta domestic unit revenue +16% and Q4 seats under 2% (rttnews above). Alaska September yield +17% (ALK 8-K above). AAL route exits (https://liveandletsfly.com/american-airlines-q3-2026-earnings-preview/). Shares the 16 Sept Reuters piece with finding 2.

findings.finding: Balance sheet: total debt $34.7bn, stockholders' deficit $3.97bn and liquidity $11.3bn at end-Q2. With FY EPS likely turning to a loss on about $1bn+ of extra Q4 fuel, the free-cash-flow outlook and the debt-reduction path are at risk of a downgrade on the call. AAL is the most levered equity of the big three, so FCF commentary carries more weight here than at DAL or UAL.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable in the baseline; leverage was cited in the 2025 downgrades (Goldman Sell at $8, April 2025), per older coverage.
findings.why_not_priced: The debt figures are public, and the stock's -23% YTD (against DAL +8%) reflects leverage. What is not public is the new FCF number. Delta cut its FCF to about $2.5bn from $3-4bn. If AAL's FCF turn negative were priced, the stock would not have joined the UAL rally today. Note there is no new financing event, so lesson 4 does not apply.
findings.independence: Delta's FCF cut (rttnews above) is the peer analogue. The debt figures share a document with finding 4's capacity data (Live and Let's Fly cites $28.9bn LTD and $3.1bn current).

findings.finding: Leadership pressure is unresolved: the flight attendants' union passed its first-ever vote of no confidence in CEO Robert Isom, and the pilots' union pressed the board for 'decisive action' (reported 18 Sept 2026). AAL reshuffled its commercial and operations leadership on 13 Aug 2026. A management change announced with the print would be a positive catalyst, but no source says one is scheduled.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a low-probability event. If the market expected a change, the commentary would carry dated board-level reporting, and none was found after September.
findings.independence: Executive reshuffle (https://www.airliners.de/gewinndruck-american-airlines-baut-fuehrungsteam/89597, 2026-08-13). One Mile at a Time on the union no-confidence vote (https://onemileatatime.com/news/american-ceo-robert-isom-turnaround-plan/); the date was not confirmed from its URL.
